reference: GNU coreutils tee is the independent oracle for parity cases, run by system Bash with the same bounded fixture script. The runner verifies each expected reference status before comparing stdout bytes and the complete private fixture tree. Contract expectations come from Bash type/help behavior and the documented tee synopsis/options in the stock Bash loadable source.
coverage: Binary and unterminated input copied to stdout and multiple files
Empty input creates empty output files
Overwrite truncates an existing file while retaining its mode
Append mode preserves prior bytes and creates additional outputs
End-of-options handling for a relative filename beginning with a dash
A failed output open is reported while healthy outputs still receive input
Invalid option and closed-stdin error statuses
Bash builtin availability and documented help metadata
exclusions: SIGINT behavior for -i is deferred because this runner has no controlled per-process signal scheduler.
Per-sink write-error recovery is deferred because this runner does not provide a deterministic private write-fault injection sink; /dev/full is not used.
No live terminal, device, host path, or external process signal is exercised.

cases.purpose: Copy NUL-containing input without a final newline to stdout and two output files.
EOF on the runner-provided empty stdin should still create each named output as an empty file.
Overwrite truncates existing contents; its existing mode remains unchanged despite a later umask change.
cases.script: umask 077; printf 'old contents\n' > target; umask 022; printf 'new\n' | tee target

cases.purpose: Combined -a and -i options append binary input to an existing file and create a second output; absent a signal, bytes match GNU tee.
cases.script: printf 'prefix:' > existing; printf '\000tail' | tee -ai existing added

cases.purpose: The -- option terminator permits tee to create a relative file whose name begins with a dash.
A missing-parent output reports failure but must not prevent stdout or a later healthy file from receiving the full input.
Check GNU tee's exit status and diagnostic policy for an unrecognized option; preserve a candidate status difference as a failure.
A closed standard input descriptor is a read error and should return the GNU tee failure status.
Bash type metadata identifies tee as a builtin when the executable search path is empty.
The Bash help text exposes the documented synopsis and the append and interrupt options described by the stock tee loadable documentation.
cases.script: PATH=; doc=$(help tee); [[ $doc == *"tee [-ai] [file ...]"* && $doc == *appended* && $doc == *"ignores interrupts"* ]]; printf 'help exposes synopsis and -a/-i documentation\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise the documented difference between tee and tee -i when SIGINT arrives during a blocked bounded read.
Exercise recovery when one already-open output fails during write while other output descriptors remain healthy.
Repeated calls use fresh stdin and recover after a failed output open; diagnostics remain visible.
cases.script:
printf 'one\000tail' > input
tee first < input
if tee absent/failed second < input; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi
printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"
tee third < input
